pharm: Synthetic nonapeptide identical to endogenous oxytocin; binds myometrial oxytocin receptors to increase intracellular calcium and stimulate rhythmic uterine contractions
quick: Induction: dilute infusion start 0.5-1 mU/min, titrate; PPH control: per protocol IV/IM after delivery
Used intrapartum only for medically indicated induction/augmentation; not for elective induction
Compatible; endogenous hormone, supports milk let-down
No specific dose adjustment; watch fluid balance (antidiuretic effect)
Continuous uterine activity and fetal heart rate, maternal BP/pulse, fluid balance
summary: Oxytocin (Pitocin) is a synthetic uterotonic used intravenously, with adequate medical supervision in hospital, for medically indicated induction or augmentation of labor, as adjunct in incomplete/inevitable abortion, and (postpartum) to produce uterine contraction and control postpartum bleeding. It is NOT indicated for elective induction of labor because the benefit-to-risk data are inadequate. Dose is individualized to uterine response, started at a very low rate and titrated. Key hazards are uterine hyperstimulation/rupture, fetal distress, and - because oxytocin has intrinsic antidiuretic activity - water intoxication with convulsions and coma when large doses are infused over prolonged periods.
indications: Induction of labor when there is a medical indication (e.g. Rh problems, maternal diabetes, preeclampsia at/near term, premature rupture of membranes with indicated delivery)
Stimulation/reinforcement of labor in selected cases of uterine inertia
Adjunctive therapy in the management of incomplete or inevitable abortion
Postpartum: to produce uterine contraction in the third stage of labor and to control postpartum bleeding or hemorrhage

dosage.r: IV infusion (drip, only acceptable route for this use)
dosage.d: Standard solution 10 units in 1000 mL (10 mU/mL); start 0.5-1 mU/min, increase by 1-2 mU/min every 30-60 min until adequate contraction pattern
dosage.n: Reduce dose once labor established (~5-6 cm); rates >9-10 mU/min rarely needed; give higher rates with great care

dosage.d: 10-40 units added to 1000 mL of a nonhydrating diluent, infused at a rate that controls uterine atony
10 units in 500 mL diluent at ~20-40 mU/min (per protocol)
dosage.n: Curettage is primary therapy in first trimester

admin: For induction/augmentation, IV infusion (drip method) by infusion pump is the only acceptable parenteral route; piggyback onto a physiologic electrolyte solution so it can be stopped abruptly
Administer only with adequate medical supervision in a hospital
Inspect solution for particulate matter/discoloration; rotate the bottle to mix thoroughly
Continuously monitor uterine activity, resting tone and fetal heart rate; stop infusion for hyperstimulation or fetal distress
moa: Promotes uterine contraction by binding specific myometrial oxytocin receptors (whose concentration rises greatly in pregnancy, peaking in early labor at term) and increasing intracellular calcium, which drives actomyosin contraction via myosin light-chain kinase. In pure form it also has intrinsic pressor and antidiuretic (vasopressin-like) activity at high doses.

absolute: Unfavorable fetal positions/presentations undeliverable without conversion (e.g. transverse lie)
Fetal distress where delivery is not imminent
Conditions where vaginal delivery is contraindicated (invasive cervical carcinoma, active genital herpes, total placenta previa, vasa previa, cord presentation/prolapse)
monitor: Uterine contraction frequency, strength and resting tone

preg: Oxytocin is used during pregnancy only intrapartum for medically indicated induction/augmentation; it is NOT indicated for elective induction of labor (inadequate benefit-risk data). It is not expected to cause fetal structural abnormalities; fetal/neonatal risks relate to induced uterine activity (bradycardia, low Apgar, jaundice, hemorrhage) and excessive dosing.
lact: Oxytocin is an endogenous hormone involved in milk ejection; small amounts may appear in milk but it is considered compatible with breastfeeding and is rapidly degraded in the infant GI tract.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment, but its antidiuretic effect predisposes to water retention/hyponatremia - limit volume of hypotonic fluids and monitor fluid balance, especially with prolonged infusion.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment; oxytocin is rapidly cleared by the liver and kidney.

major: Prostaglandins (e.g. misoprostol, dinoprostone) - potentiate uterine activity; risk of hyperstimulation/rupture, avoid simultaneous use
Vasoconstrictors given with caudal block anesthesia - severe hypertension reported 3-4 hours later
moderate: Cyclopropane anesthesia - may modify cardiovascular effects (hypotension, maternal sinus bradycardia with abnormal AV rhythm)
minor: Drugs prolonging QT - theoretical additive effect
interactions.alcohol: Not applicable in the obstetric setting
interactions.diagnostics: Prolonged high-dose infusion can cause dilutional hyponatremia (water intoxication) - monitor electrolytes

serious: Uterine hypertonicity, spasm, tetanic contraction or rupture of the uterus
Severe water intoxication with convulsions and coma (and maternal death reported)
emergency: Sustained uterine tetany or suspected uterine rupture
Fetal distress / abnormal fetal heart rate
Seizures or coma from water intoxication

monitoring: Continuous fetal heart rate and uterine activity (frequency, strength, resting tone) during induction/augmentation
Fluid intake and output; serum electrolytes with prolonged or high-dose infusion (water intoxication)
Signs of uterine hyperstimulation - stop infusion if they occur
Postpartum: uterine tone and blood loss

The drip may be slowed or stopped if contractions become too strong or your baby's heart rate changes

It is not used to start labor electively without a medical reason
Used after delivery it helps the womb contract and reduces bleeding
pk: IV: uterine response almost immediate; IM: within 3-5 minutes
About 1-6 minutes (shorter in late pregnancy and lactation)
IV effect subsides within ~1 hour of stopping; IM effect persists 2-3 hours

pearls: APPROPRIATE USE: Pitocin is NOT indicated for ELECTIVE induction of labor (no medical indication) - reserve for medically indicated induction/augmentation; available data are inadequate to support elective use
Give only by controlled IV infusion (pump) with continuous fetal/uterine monitoring, in a hospital - piggyback so it can be stopped abruptly
Oxytocin has intrinsic antidiuretic (vasopressin-like) activity - prolonged high-dose infusion (40-50 mU/min) with large hypotonic fluid volumes can cause fatal water intoxication
Stop the infusion immediately for uterine hyperstimulation, tetanic contractions or fetal distress
missed: Not applicable - oxytocin is administered by clinicians as a titrated infusion or single peripartum dose, not self-administered. Infusion rate is adjusted by staff according to uterine and fetal response.
overdose: Overdose causes uterine hyperstimulation - hypertonic/tetanic contractions, tumultuous labor, uterine rupture, cervical/vaginal lacerations, postpartum hemorrhage, uteroplacental hypoperfusion and fetal hypoxia/death. Water intoxication with convulsions can occur from the antidiuretic effect with large prolonged doses. Management: immediately discontinue oxytocin and provide symptomatic and supportive therapy (restrict free water, correct hyponatremia, manage uterine atony/hemorrhage).
